findings.text: Tested on an emulated FM-1 with the newer UC25HQ80 flash chip: it stops using its flash there (on the original chip it saves). On newer FM-1 units its settings would be lost at power-off and later installs refused, which then needs a USB download-mode rescue. Check the project for a newer release.

From the code alone: Checks for the original Puya flash chip only. On newer FM-1 units (UC25HQ80 flash) firmware like this has kept saves in RAM only and refused later installs, which then needs a USB download-mode rescue. Check the project's notes for newer-unit support before installing on a recent FM-1.
Does not pose as a keyboard, mouse or drive over USB.

brick.reason: Saves to flash on the original chip (2 writes) but never on the UC25HQ80: changes would be kept in RAM only and lost at power-off.
